metadata.note: The Charleston and Western Carolina Railway (1896) and the companies before it on its corridors: Port Royal Railroad (1871-78), Port Royal and Augusta (1878-96), Augusta and Knoxville (1882-83), Port Royal and Western Carolina (1886-96). Drawn from research/branches/charleston_and_western_carolina_railway.txt in the site repo (DanielMConnolly/historical-trains), researched 2026-11-05. Only the report's drawable spans are drawn. Rule 4 splits share geometry per corridor: each slice of Augusta - Yemassee - Port Royal and Augusta - Greenwood - Laurens - Spartanburg comes from one traced line. Atlantic Coast Line control from 1897 is a stock matter and not a split; no ACL feature, because no C&WC passenger train is known to have survived to the merger of 31 Dec 1959. Not drawn: Augusta Terminal Railway, Angle Siding, Glenn Springs Railroad, and a separate Augusta - Parksville 1881 span. Rule 1: passengers did not leave the C&WC all at once, so the Spartanburg, Anderson and Greenville lines stop well before Port Royal's.
metadata.open_ends: [OPEN] last-confirmed-year ends, not endings: Augusta - Yemassee and Yemassee - Port Royal 1954; Augusta - Greenwood, Greenwood - Laurens and Laurens - Spartanburg 1932; Anderson Branch 1946; Greenville Branch 1924. [OPEN] start: PR&WC Anderson Branch 1889.
not_yet_sourced: OPEN END, main line mixed trains: coach on freight from 8 Feb 1932 is proven; the end is unknown except daggered by Sept 1951. Augusta - Greenwood, Greenwood - Laurens and Laurens - Spartanburg are drawn only to 1932.
OPEN END, Greenville Branch: last proof Aug 1924, freight-only by 1951. The most thinly sourced line.
OPEN END, Anderson Branch: bracket Aug 1946 - Sept 1951.
OPEN END, Port Royal: 1954 / 1955 / by 1957 from three secondary sources, none citing a notice; Dec 1954 and Dec 1957 Guides would settle it.

OPERATOR UNCERTAIN: Greenwood - Spartanburg 1885-86 is drawn under the Port Royal and Augusta by inference; no timetable was seen, and the Greenwood, Laurens and Spartanburg or the Augusta and Knoxville may have been the name on the train.
OPEN START: Port Royal and Western Carolina Anderson Branch, 1889 is first proven against ICC completion in 1886.
Recruit trains to Parris Island after the public trains ended: unconfirmed, road or rail unknown, not drawn. Angle Siding (military, 1959 Guide) not drawn.

Whether the Clark Hill (J. Strom Thurmond) Reservoir, about 1946-54, moved or raised the main line near Clarks Hill - Parksville - Plum Branch - McCormick and the Anderson Branch near Bordeaux - Mount Carmel: no relocation notice found; one abandonedrails.com photo caption says the Anderson Branch grade was apparently raised.
Greenwood - Laurens traces 10% under Fowler's mileage while Laurens - Spartanburg traces 4% over; the depot's milepost at the split is unresolved.
headway_min and avg_speed_kmh are estimates throughout; only the 1889-derived speeds rest on a timetable, and that OCR is partly garbled.
Date assignment of two Laurens Advertiser clips (mixed train about 1906, chair cars 1914) comes from a newsletter's caption order and is not used in a segment.
source_conflicts: Port Royal line end: Wikipedia C&WC 'between 1954 and 1957' citing the Official Guide of Dec 1954 and Dec 1957; Wikipedia Augusta Union Station 'between 1954 and 1955'; Great Union Stations '1955' with nothing in its 1956 column. Drawn to 1954 as last confirmed.

Central of Georgia 1881-94: Wikipedia says the lines were 'operated as part of' the Central; 1888-89 ads run under the PR&A and PR&WC names. Held as no split; an 1880s Official Guide would re-check it.
Port Royal Railroad opening: ICC 1871/1873; Beaufort District Collection 1 Mar 1873; a search-surfaced 9 Mar 1874 for full completion, not read. Drawn 1871 to Almeda and 1873 beyond.
Augusta and Knoxville lease: Wikipedia says to the PR&A, the Hub City newsletter says the Central.
Greenville and Laurens completion: Wikipedia and a blog 1882 / 1884; the 1885 press still has it waiting for iron; ICC 8 Sep 1886 preferred.
ACL control date: 1897 (Wikipedia, RailGA), 1898 (abandonedrails), Feb 1908 ACL Company (American-Rails). Irrelevant to the map.
metadata.known_defect_elsewhere: columbia_upstate.geojson's 'Southern Railway: Columbia – Greenville' sits on this layer's Laurens - Greenville alignment (report EXISTING LAYER CHECK). Left unchanged here; flagged for its own fix.

segments.note: C&WC from the corporate transfer of 3 Oct 1896. Nos. 41/42, one daily each way by 1942; the Dec 1951 table in the Feb 1952 Official Guide still prints them ('Augusta, Beaufort and Port Royal') and the index does not dagger these stations. End: Wikipedia's Official Guide citation has the train running Dec 1954 with an end between 1954 and 1957; Wikipedia's Augusta Union Station says between 1954 and 1955; Great Union Stations says 1955. The last primary sighting read directly is the Dec 1951 table. This is the last CONFIRMED year, not a known end. Do not extend without evidence. headway_min is an estimate from the 1942 count: service was heavier earlier. ACL's own Augusta trains used Robbins - Augusta from 1 Dec 1899; ACL control from 1897 is a stock matter, so no split.

Greenwood: approximated straight leg 1.04 mi through town between the mapped C&WC abandoned ways (34.181, -82.167 to 34.1955, -82.163), no surviving trace. The 2.0 mi south of it (34.161 to 34.179) uses untagged CSX yard track beside the Monroe Subdivision, with 0.2 mi of a track OSM tags SAL at the yard throat. Augusta end: drawn to the junction of the CSX Augusta and McCormick Subdivisions at 33.4666, -81.9653, about 0.4 mi from the Union Station site (33.4715, -81.9685; station opened 1903 and is demolished); both Augusta lines share this anchor. Any reservoir-era relocation or raising of this stretch would therefore be in the drawn line and not in the era's. Whether it was moved is UNRESOLVED: OSM has no old-alignment way here (it does for the SAL at Russell Lake), OHM has only a coarse Atack-dataset way south of Pollards, and the newspaper search found no relocation notice. No part of this line lies in the OSM lake polygon.

segments.note: Regular trains Nos. 1 and 4 Augusta - Spartanburg: C&WC notice of 26 Jan 1932, last trips Saturday 6 Feb 1932. From 8 Feb 1932 a coach rode tri-weekly freights (McCormick Messenger 11 Feb 1932: 'Mixed passenger service on the Main line'), so passengers demonstrably continued past 1932 for an unknown time, before Sept 1951 when the Feb 1952 Official Guide index daggers this line's stations freight-only. Drawn to 1932 only because no later year is confirmed. This is the last CONFIRMED year, not a known end. Do not extend without evidence. Coach on freights Nos. 17/18 used Green Street Crossing at Augusta and the freight station at Greenwood. Plum Branch and McCormick are daggered in the 1952 Guide index. headway_min is an estimate for Nos. 1/4 before 1932.
sources: Segment-level: the report cites the McCormick Messenger of 28 Jan and 11 Feb 1932, the Feb 1952 Guide index and the Hub City newsletter.

Approximated straight legs: Bordeaux 0.53 mi (33.924, -82.371 to 33.920, -82.379, gap in the mapped grade); river valley south of Lowndesville 1.72 mi (34.167, -82.624 to 34.190, -82.634), about 0.9 mi of which lies in today's Richard B. Lifted line: the drawn route is the OSM mapping of the abandoned grade, including stretches now under Huguenot Parkway.

segments.note: NOT ended by the Feb 1932 cut: a mixed train still ran. Mar 1931 'a mixed train, carrying passenger, express and mail, freight' McCormick - Anderson; No. 21 mixed except Sunday and Nos. 5/6 Sunday-only, May 1931; Nos. 5/6 off 7 Feb 1932; engineer on 'the mixed train' 8 Aug 1946. The 1952 Guide daggers the stations, so service ended between Aug 1946 and Sept 1951. This is the last CONFIRMED year, not a known end. Do not extend without evidence. McCormick - Iva abandonment in the late 1970s and Iva - South Anderson in the early 1980s are not passenger dates. headway_min is an estimate.
sources: Segment-level: the report cites the McCormick Messenger of 1931, 1932 and 1946 and the Guide index; abandonedrails is cited for abandonment only.
